title: Persecution and Divine Deliverance
english: Isaiah declares that God will heal many and bring comfort to those who are afflicted.
Isaiah says, 'Strengthen your weak hands and feeble knees; encourage those who are faint-hearted, and do not be afraid' (Isaiah 35:3-4).

Furthermore, Isaiah promises that God will come and bring light to those in darkness, that the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear; then the lame will leap with joy like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will speak clearly (Isaiah 35:5-6).
Isaiah also says that God will raise the dead and wipe away every tear from every face (Isaiah 25:8).
Isaiah asks, 'Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?' (Isaiah 53:1).
He answers, 'They will see to whom no report has been made, and those who have not heard will understand' (Isaiah 52:15).
Isaiah additionally says that on the day of the Lord's coming, people will say, 'Behold, our God; we have waited for him, and he will give us rest' (Isaiah 25:9).

Zechariah speaks of this day, saying, 'Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout, daughter of Jerusalem, for your king is coming to you, righteous and humble, riding on a donkey and a young colt' (Zechariah 9:9).
Jacob says, 'He ties his donkey to the vine' (Genesis 49:11).
Malachi says, 'Suddenly the Lord will come to his temple, the messenger of the covenant' (Malachi 3:1).
David says in the Psalms, 'I will prepare praise from the mouth of infants and nursing babies' (Psalm 8:2).

The Lord will rebuke the people, as Malachi says, for he will draw near to them in judgment and will be a swift witness against those who practice sorcery, against the adulteresses, and against those who swear falsely (Malachi 3:5).
Jeremiah also says that the Lord's house should not be a den of robbers, and his name should not be called upon them (Jeremiah 7:11).
The Lord will be anointed with perfume, as it is written in the Songs, until the king is on his throne and the perfume gives its fragrance (Song of Solomon 1:12).

The Lord's enemies will gather against him, as David says in the second Psalm, for the nations will rage and the peoples will devise empty things, and the kings of the earth stood, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ (Psalm 2:1-2).
David also says in the third Psalm: 'Lord, why have those afflicting me multiplied? Many rise up against me; many say to my soul: There is no salvation for him in his God' (Psalm 3:1-2).
Jeremiah says: 'The Spirit before our face, Christ the Lord, was taken in our corruptions' (Psalm 41:4-5).
He also says: 'We did not say: We will live in his shadow' (Psalm 41:4-5).
They devised words for my capture and laid snares for me (Psalm 41:4-5).
The Lord knew all their counsel against me unto death; do not acquit their injustices, and do not wipe out their sins from your face (Psalm 41:8-9).

They will bear false witness against me - David in the 35th Psalm says: Witnesses rose up against me, unjust ones, of which I had no knowledge, they asked me; they repaid me evil for good (Psalm 35:11).
David again says in the 59th Psalm: Deliver me from my enemies, O God, and from those rising up against me, redeem me (Psalm 59:1-2).
Rescue me from those working lawlessness and save me from men of blood (Psalm 59:2).
My enemies said bad things to me, when will he die and his name perish? (Psalm 41:5).
They came to see, speaking vainly (Psalm 41:6).
Their heart gathered lawlessness, going out and speaking (Psalm 41:6).
All my enemies whispered against me, thinking bad things against me, placing a lawless word against me (Psalm 41:7).
The one eating my bread magnified a heel against me (Psalm 41:9).
Why does the strong one boast in evil, lawlessness all day? (Psalm 50:3).
His tongue thought injustice (Psalm 50:2).
He made deceit like a sharpened razor, loved evil more than goodness (Psalm 50:2-3).
My friends and those near me stood against me (Psalm 55:12-13).
The words of Judas will be, 'Hail, rabbi' (Matthew 26:49).
David says, 'His words were smoother than oil, but they are arrows' (Psalm 55:21).
Cast your care upon the Lord and he will sustain you (Psalm 55:22).
Do not be silent, God, of my praise, for the mouth of the sinner and the mouth of the deceitful opened against me (Psalm 109:2).
Zechariah says, 'I will say to them, if it is good in your sight, give my wage, thirty pieces of silver' (Zechariah 11:12-13).

title: The Suffering Servant in Prophecy
english: The prophet Jeremiah says that they gave thirty silver pieces, the price of the valued one whom they valued from the sons of Israel, and they gave them for the potter's field (Jeremiah 45:2).
Isaiah says, 'Woe to your soul, because you have taken counsel against yourselves, saying, Let us bind the righteous man, for he is troublesome to us' (Isaiah 46:1).
Solomon says, 'Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, for he is troublesome and a burden to us' (Isaiah 46:2).
David says in the 69th Psalm, 'Save me, O God, for waters have come up to my soul; I have sunk in deep mire, and there is no standing' (Psalm 47:1).
Again, David says in the 71st Psalm, 'I have hoped in you, Lord; let me not be ashamed forever. In your righteousness rescue me and deliver me' (Psalm 47:2).
Isaiah asks, 'Why did you open your mouth? And why did you loosen your tongue? Except against the meek and humble and quiet?' (Isaiah 47:3).

Again, Isaiah says, 'My inheritance has become like a lion in the forest; it gave its voice against me, therefore I hated it. I did not reject it, but they rejected me; therefore I abandoned my house' (Isaiah 47:4).
Micah says, 'They will strike the judge of Israel on the cheek' (Isaiah 48:1).
He will be despised by the nations; kings will see him and rise up and bow down to him (Isaiah 48:2).
And elsewhere he says, 'I gave my back to scourges, my cheeks to blows, and my face I did not turn away from shameful spitting' (Isaiah 48:3).
The apostles will flee (Isaiah 49:t).
David says in the 67th Psalm, 'My friends and those near me stood against me' (Isaiah 49:1).
Again, he says, 'You made my acquaintances distant from me' (Isaiah 49:2).
And, 'I sought a sympathizer, but there was none, and one calling out, but I did not find' (Isaiah 49:3).
Peter will deny (Isaiah 50:t).
Isaiah says, 'And he feared from mortal man, who will wither like grass, but the Lord says he forgot me' (Isaiah 50:1).
They will crucify him (Isaiah 51:t).
Jeremiah says, 'I, like an innocent lamb, am being led to be sacrificed' (Isaiah 51:1).
Isaiah says, 'Like a sheep to slaughter he was led, and like a lamb before his shearer, he was silent' (Isaiah 51:2).
Wisdom says, 'Let us condemn him to an inglorious death' (Isaiah 51:3).
Again, 'Come, let us put wood into his bread and let us trip him up from the land of the living' (Isaiah 51:4).
David says, 'They pierced my hands and my feet' (Isaiah 51:5).
They will crown him with thorns (Isaiah 52:t).
David says in the 69th Psalm, 'They gave me gall for my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink' (Isaiah 53:1).
Moses says, 'Do you repay the Lord for these things?' (Isaiah 53:2).
In the Songs, it is said, 'He entered my garden, my sister, my bride; and they harvested my myrrh' (Isaiah 53:3).
'My hands dripped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of myrrh' (Isaiah 53:4).
Again, he says, 'I will give you to drink from the wine of myrrh' (Isaiah 53:5).
Isaiah says that the one coming from Edom will wear a red garment, and his red clothing is from Bozrah; he is beautiful in his attire with might (Isaiah 54:1).
David says that he became like a man who does not hear and does not have rebukes in his mouth (Isaiah 55:1).
Again, David says, 'I have become like a deaf man who does not hear, and like a mute who does not open his mouth' (Isaiah 55:2).

Isaiah also says that because he was afflicted, he does not open his mouth; like a sheep led to slaughter and a lamb before its shearer, so he will not open his mouth in his humiliation (Isaiah 55:3).
David says that they saw him and shook their heads (Isaiah 56:1).
And Wisdom says that if he is the Son of God, he will be rescued (Isaiah 56:2).
Moses says, 'Your life shall be hung on a tree in the presence of your eyes, and you will be afraid day and night...' (Isaiah 57:1)
translator_notes: The text ends mid-sentence with a trailing ellipsis, indicating that it is incomplete.
The Greek text of Jeremiah 45.2 contains the word τετιμημενος, which is translated as 'valued one' in the English translation.
The reference to Isaiah 63:1-3 is included based on the Greek description of the one coming from Edom in red garments from Bozrah.
The Moses reference at 57.1 is a reference to the law found in Deuteronomy 21:22-23.
baehrens: PG 41-43; Testimonia ex divinis et sacris scripturis (Khazarzar) u02 rem mid

title: Christ's Passion and Resurrection
english: At night, you will not trust in your life. Everyone who hangs on a tree is cursed, as stated in the scriptures (Deuteronomy 21:23). Isaiah cries out, saying that we considered the Messiah to be in pain and in a blow, but he was actually wounded for our iniquities and bruised for our sins, for the discipline of our peace was upon him, and by his bruise, we were all healed. Isaiah also says that the Messiah was wounded for our iniquities and bruised for our sins (Isaiah 53:5). Sirach says, 'They struck me, and I did not labor' (Sirach 51:1). David, in the 33rd Psalm, says that the blows of children became their blows (Psalm 33).

The Lord also says that in the night, when it is cold and coal is laid, Christ will suffer. Zechariah says that it will be cold and frost will be for one day. The sun will set, and Zechariah first says that there will not be light on that day, but the Lord knows that day, and it is not day or night, and towards evening, there will be light. Joel also says that before the Lord's face, the earth will be gathered, and the heaven will be darkened; the sun and moon will be darkened, and the stars will pour out their light. Amos says that the sun will set at noon, and it will be dark on the earth on the day of its light, and he will turn our festivals into mourning.

As the scriptures foretell, Christ's passion will be marked by his clothes being divided, as David says in the 22nd Psalm, 'They divided my clothes among themselves and cast a lot for my garment' (Psalm 22:18). He will be crucified with robbers, and Isaiah says that he was reckoned with the lawless and his soul was handed over to death. They will pierce his side, as Zacharias prophesied, saying, 'They will look upon the one they pierced' (Zechariah 12:10). His bone will not be broken, as Moses said, 'A bone of his will not be broken' (Exodus 12:46, Numbers 9:12, Psalm 34:20). Water will flow from his side as a type of baptism, and Isaiah says, 'Bread will be given to him, and his water is faithful' (Isaiah 30:20-21).

Christ will be placed in a rock, as Isaiah foretold, saying, 'Look at the solid rock, which you quarried, and at the pit of the cistern, which you dug' (Isaiah 51:1-2). The stone is the door of the tomb, and the same one says, 'And they placed a stone on me'. Daniel said that the king would seal the stone with his ring and the ring of his nobles, so that nothing may be changed in Daniel. The time of Christ's passion will be at the beginning of summer, in the month of March, as indicated in the Songs, which says, 'The time has passed; the nations have gone their way. He appeared on earth, the time of harvest has arrived' (Song of Solomon 2:11-12).

Ultimately, Christ will be buried, as Isaiah said, 'The righteous one was taken away from the face of injustice. His burial will be in peace' (Isaiah 57:1-2). And again, Isaiah says, 'He was led to death because of the sins of my people. And I will give the wicked in exchange for his burial and the rich in exchange for his death' (Isaiah 53:8-9). Jacob says, 'He lay down and fell asleep like a lion and like a cub. Who will arouse him?' (Genesis 49:9). And in Numbers, it is said, 'Lying down, he rested like a lion and like a cub' (Numbers 23:24). David, in one of his Psalms, says, 'You led me to the dust of death' (Psalm 22:15).

Christ, who is sinless, will terrify Hades and be buried. As it is written in Job, 'The gates of death will be opened to him with fear, and the gatekeepers of Hades, seeing him, spat' (Job 38:17). Isaiah also says, 'Hades was embittered, meeting you below' (Isaiah 14:15). In another Psalm, David says, 'He broke the bronze gates and shattered the iron bars' (Psalm 107:16). This is because Christ is sinless, as Isaiah writes, saying, 'Who did not commit sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth' (Isaiah 53:9). And again, Isaiah says, 'He was led to death because of the sins of my people' (Isaiah 53:8).

Christ's descent into Hades is also mentioned in other Psalms. For example, David says, 'Because of the affliction of the poor and the groaning of the needy, now I will rise, says the Lord' (Psalm 12:5). Additionally, David writes, 'For you will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will you give your holy one to see corruption' (Psalm 16:10). Jeremiah also mentions Christ's resurrection, saying, 'Therefore I awoke, and behold, my sleep was sweet' (Jeremiah 31:26). David, in another Psalm, says, 'I cried out to God by day and by night, and was reckoned with those going down to the pit' (Psalm 88:1). He also says, 'I became like…'
And David in the 34th Psalm says, 'The Lord redeems the soul of his servants, and none of those who take refuge in him will be condemned' (Psalm 34:22).
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the edges.
The translation of 'ἐπικατάρατος' as 'cursed' is accurate, but the context of the curse is important to understand.
The verb 'ἐλογισάμεθα' is translated as 'considered', which is the most accurate translation in this context.
The word 'παideία' is translated as 'discipline', which is the correct translation in this context.
The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the end.
The translation aims to preserve the original word order and meaning, while also conveying the author's intended message in natural literary prose.
The translation of 'ἐγκαταλείψεις' as 'abandon' is chosen over 'leave' for contextual reasons.
The translation of 'ἀναστήσεται' as 'will rise' is chosen over 'rise' for grammatical reasons.
Some biblical references may be mistranslated or not entirely accurate.
The final fragment 'Ἐγενήθην ὡσεὶ' is translated as 'I became like…' and is included at the end of the text.
